name: College Dorm Checklist
description: A room-by-room list of essentials to furnish and set up a college dorm.

items.text: Add a mattress topper sized to your dorm bed.
items.note: Confirm whether your bed is a standard or extra-long twin first.

items.text: Set up sheets, a comforter and pillows.
Hang or clip a small reading light by the bed.
Add a bed riser set to create under-bed storage.
Keep a water bottle and tissues within reach.
Use a fan or small heater allowed by your dorm.
Set up a desk lamp with adjustable brightness.
Add a desk organizer for pens and supplies.
Bring a comfortable chair cushion if seating is hard.
Use a corkboard or whiteboard for reminders.
Add a power strip with surge protection and USB ports.
Keep a small wastebasket beside the desk.
Use stackable bins and under-bed containers.
Add closet organizers, hangers and shelf dividers.
Hang an over-the-door rack for shoes or supplies.
Use drawer organizers for small items.
Add command hooks for bags, keys and towels.
Label bins so you can find things fast.
Add a mini-fridge if your dorm allows one.
Bring a microwave or use a shared one.
items.note: Check wattage and size limits in your housing rules.

items.text: Pack a few plates, bowls, cups and utensils.
Add a reusable water bottle and travel mug.
Bring snacks and a small set of food storage containers.
Include dish soap, a sponge and paper towels.
Stock all-purpose cleaner and disinfecting wipes.
Add a small broom, dustpan and trash bags.
Bring a laundry hamper or bag and detergent.
Include a stain remover and dryer sheets.
Keep air freshener for a small shared space.
Add a roll of paper towels and tissues.
Add a rug to soften the floor and define the space.
Hang posters, photos or removable wall art.
Use string lights or a lamp for warm lighting.
Add throw pillows and a cozy blanket.
Place a small mirror near the door or desk.
Include a few plants or simple personal touches.

faq.q: What are the most important dorm room essentials?
faq.a: Prioritize a good mattress topper and bedding, storage bins, a desk lamp, a power strip and basic cleaning supplies. These items have the biggest impact on comfort and function in a small room.

faq.q: What should I share with my roommate?
faq.a: Coordinate large or duplicate items like a mini-fridge, microwave, rug, trash can and decor. Splitting these saves money and prevents a cramped room full of doubles.

faq.q: Are mini-fridges and microwaves allowed in dorms?
faq.a: Often yes, but size limits and rules vary by school, and some dorms provide them. Check your housing guidelines before buying any appliance so it isn't turned away on move-in day.

faq.q: How do I make a small dorm room feel bigger?
faq.a: Use vertical and under-bed storage, keep surfaces clear, add a mirror, and choose light, layered lighting. Multi-purpose furniture and good organization make a tight room feel open.

faq.q: Can I download this checklist as a PDF?
faq.a: Yes. Print the checklist or download the PDF and tick off each item as you furnish and set up your dorm room.
